extracted.intended_audience: very large financial institutions; banks and payments providers; consumer advocates; legal and compliance professionals; members of the public interested in CFPB rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Landing page summarizing the CFPB final rule that amends Regulations E and Z to update regulatory exceptions for overdraft credit provided by very large financial institutions, with publication and docket metadata and stated policy objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Regulations E and Z
rubrics_metrics.description: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau amends Regulations E (12 CFR Part 1005) and Z (12 CFR Part 1026) to update regulatory exceptions for overdraft credit provided by very large financial institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the specific regulatory parts being changed (12 CFR Part 1005 and 1026) and points readers to the full final rule (PDF and Federal Register notice) for the detailed regulatory text and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — applies to overdraft credit by very large financial institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule targets overdraft credit provided by very large financial institutions (VLFI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The landing page identifies the affected actor class (VLFIs) — further details on which institutions qualify and how the rule applies to them are in the full rule text and docket (CFPB-2024-0002).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity with consumer protections for similarly situated products
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of overdraft credit must adhere to consumer protections required of similarly situated consumer credit products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule's intent is to align overdraft credit regulatory treatment with that of comparable credit products; the full rule will specify which statutory/regulatory protections are applied or clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-fee exception — fee limited to recovery of estimated costs and losses
rubrics_metrics.description: An exception remains when the overdraft fee is a small amount that only recovers estimated costs and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This carve-out is based on the fee's purpose and magnitude rather than an automatic exemption; the landing summary does not provide numeric thresholds — the final rule text should be consulted for any definitional or measurement guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-facing objective — improve comparison shopping
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule is intended to allow consumers to better comparison shop across credit products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an articulated policy goal/outcome of the rule; supporting explanations and examples of how disclosures or coverage changes enable comparison shopping will be in the full regulatory text and preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural and publication metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative details: Date issued by CFPB (DEC 12, 2024), Federal Register publication date (DEC 30, 2024), Federal Register citation (89 FR 106768), effective date (OCT 01, 2025), docket number (CFPB-2024-0002), RIN (3170-AA42).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metadata items specify the official record, timeline, and identifiers for compliance and for submitting/comments (where applicable). Consult the Federal Register notice and docket for rule text, regulatory analyses, and administrative timelines.
